topics.titleTr: KEDA ile Boştaki Kubernetes Maliyetini Kesin
topics.titleEn: Kill Idle Kubernetes Costs with KEDA
topics.angle: how-to|cut spend from idle and over-provisioned workloads with event-driven and scheduled scaling.
topics.brief: Grounded in the 2026 shift from k8s adoption to optimization, with idle workloads named the top waste source. Sections: find idle spend (namespace/pod-level cost attribution); scale to zero with KEDA event-driven autoscaling; park non-prod with kube-downscaler on a schedule; pair with Karpenter for right-sized nodes; guardrails so scaling-to-zero doesn't break latency SLOs. Verify tool behaviors and any cited savings. Primary sources: KubeCon EU 2026 recaps; Coralogix / SUSE Kubernetes cost-optimization guides.

topics.titleTr: Kubernetes'te AI Çıkarım GPU Maliyetini Kesin
topics.titleEn: Taming GPU Costs for AI Inference on K8s
topics.angle: deep-dive|control the GPU bill when serving generative AI inference on Kubernetes.
topics.brief: Start from the stat that a majority of orgs hosting generative models run at least some inference on Kubernetes, pushing GPU discipline onto platform teams. Sections: why GPUs break classic autoscaling (cold starts, fractional sharing); tactics (MIG/time-slicing, request batching, autoscaling on queue depth, spot GPUs with checkpointing); measuring cost-per-1k-tokens served; when managed inference beats self-hosting. Verify the two-thirds figure and GPU-sharing claims. Primary sources: Coralogix Kubernetes cost guide; CIO 'Kubernetes costs keep rising' piece.

topics.titleTr: FinOps Platform Ekibinin İşi Olduğunda
topics.titleEn: When FinOps Becomes the Platform Team's Job
topics.angle: deep-dive|argue cost ownership is moving from a separate FinOps function into platform teams.
topics.brief: Contrarian take: FinOps as a standalone team is dissolving into platform engineering in 2026. Sections: the evidence (survey data on rising TCO and AI-based cost tooling; recaps calling FinOps 'no longer separate'); what changes for platform engineers (cost as a golden-path default, showback/chargeback in the IDP, budget-aware templates); the risk of making engineers reluctant cost cops; where a central FinOps role still earns its seat. Verify the 88%/92% TCO/AI-tooling figures and the convergence claim. Primary sources: Futurum 'Platform Engineering and FinOps Converge'; CIO Kubernetes-costs piece.

topics.titleTr: CI'da Claude Code ile Otomatik Düzeltmeler
topics.titleEn: Run Claude Code in CI for Automated Fixes
topics.angle: how-to|wire Claude Code into a pipeline to auto-fix lint, flaky tests and small regressions.
topics.brief: Open with a red build fixed before the engineer finished coffee. Sections: when CI automation pays off vs noise; running Claude Code headless in a pipeline with a scoped permission mode and auto mode; safe guardrails (open a PR, never force-merge; sandboxed bash; no secret access); reviewing the bot's diffs; what to automate (formatting, obvious test fixes) vs leave to humans. Verify auto-mode/sandbox behavior and permission flags. Primary source: code.claude.com/docs/en/changelog (auto mode, Code Mode, sandbox entries).

topics.titleTr: AI Geliştiricileri Sessizce Tüketiyor mu?
topics.titleEn: Is AI Quietly Burning Out Developers?
topics.angle: deep-dive|weigh evidence that AI raises output but also a new kind of burnout, with fixes.
topics.brief: Hold two facts together: most engineers report AI improved productivity, yet studies link AI job demands to higher burnout. Sections: the paradox (more shipped, more review/oversight load, intensified pace); what a 2026 study found drives burnout (workload intensification, org pressure) and what reduces it (autonomy over how AI is used, real learning); team practices to protect focus and ownership. Verify the Oregon State study details and the productivity-survey figures. Primary sources: Oregon State AI-burnout study; TechRadar 'developers more powerful, why aren't they happy'; Thoughtworks DX post.

topics.titleTr: Kod Yazmaktan Yönetmeye: Yeni Geliştirici Rolü
topics.titleEn: From Writing Code to Steering It: New Role
topics.angle: deep-dive|map how the core dev skill is shifting from writing to planning, synthesis and review.
topics.brief: Ask what the job becomes when writing code stops being the bottleneck. Sections: the shift toward structuring a plan, reviewing AI output and synthesizing across systems as the high-value work; evidence (reports that most engineers now write less code; the 'new identity of a developer'); skills to grow deliberately (problem framing, system design, communication, taste); advice for juniors pushed into senior-shaped work early. Verify the 77%/'spend less time writing code' figures. Primary sources: GitHub Blog 'new identity of a developer'; Built In; Atlassian developer-workflow research.

topics.brief: Built on the Nov 20 2026 rollout of ChatGPT Space to Plus users 18+, replacing Library as the home for pages, slides and files. Sections: what moved and where to find things now; pages that refresh from connected apps; bringing Slides into Space; a worked example (organizing a product-launch project end to end); who has access across web/desktop/mobile. topics.titleTr: LinkedIn'de PDF Karuselleri Neden Kazanıyor?
topics.titleEn: Why PDF Carousels Win on LinkedIn Now
topics.angle: how-to|show why document posts top LinkedIn dwell time and how to build one that performs.
topics.brief: Anchor on reports that PDF/document carousels became LinkedIn's highest dwell-time format in 2026 and that the algorithm now rewards saves, comments and shares over likes, weighting the first three lines heavily. Sections: why dwell time matters; anatomy of a strong carousel (hook slide, one idea per page, a saveable payoff); posting cadence and the native-upload gotcha; measuring saves and dwell. Verify the dwell-time and ranking-signal claims; label vendor stats as unverified. Primary sources: StoryChief / Somin 2026 algorithm guides; LinkedIn's own creator updates.

topics.titleTr: TikTok Artık Arama Motoru: Ona Göre Optimize Et
topics.titleEn: TikTok Is a Search Engine: Optimize for It
topics.angle: how-to|treat TikTok as a discovery/search surface and optimize videos to be found, not just served.
topics.brief: Contrarian frame: stop chasing the For You feed and start ranking in TikTok search, which a 2026 Adobe study says consumers now use like a search engine. Sections: how TikTok surfaces searchable content (spoken keywords, on-screen text, captions, the new creator keyword controls); a keyword-first scripting workflow; evergreen 'how-to' formats that keep earning views; measuring search-driven traffic. Verify the Adobe 'TikTok as search engine' finding and the keyword-control feature. Primary sources: The Gain Blog social updates; StoryChief 2026 algorithm guide.

topics.titleTr: Instagram Artık DM Paylaşımına Göre Sıralıyor
topics.titleEn: Instagram Now Ranks You on DM Shares
topics.angle: deep-dive|unpack why sends-per-view is now a top Instagram signal and how to earn shares.
topics.brief: Lead with the 2026 claim that shares per view, especially DM sends, are among Instagram's most important ranking inputs, alongside more weight for original photos and carousels. Sections: why 'send to a friend' beats a like; content built to be shared (relatable, useful, save-and-send formats); the originality penalty for recycled/watermarked content; a check so you don't optimize for vanity reach. Verify the sends-per-view and originality-priority claims against Instagram's own statements; flag single-source stats. Primary sources: Somin / StoryChief 2026 algorithm guides; Instagram @creators updates.

topics.titleTr: Bir Haftalık Reels için ChatGPT İş Akışı
topics.titleEn: A ChatGPT Workflow for a Week of Reels
topics.angle: how-to|a repeatable ChatGPT process to plan, script and caption a week of Reels in one sitting.
topics.brief: Practical field-notes workflow for a solo creator. Sections: feed ChatGPT a brand/voice brief once and reuse it; generate a week of hooks from one content pillar; turn each hook into a 20-second script and shot list; batch captions and keyword-aware on-screen text; a human editing pass so it doesn't read as AI. Note the research point that vague prompts yield generic output, so inputs must be specific. Verify any cited feature. Primary sources: OpenAI Academy marketing use-cases; Metricool ChatGPT-for-social guide.

topics.titleTr: ChatGPT'de Bir Aylık Pazarlama Metnini Hazırla
topics.titleEn: Batch a Month of Marketing Copy in ChatGPT
topics.angle: how-to|batch-produce a month of on-brand marketing copy in a single structured ChatGPT session.
topics.brief: Show a batching session that beats one-off prompting. Sections: a prompt scaffold (role, context, task, format, constraints) reused per asset; generating a month of emails, ad variants and landing blurbs from one campaign brief; keeping voice consistent with a pasted brand profile or custom GPT; a QA checklist before anything ships; where ChatGPT shouldn't go (analytics, attribution, real-time campaign calls). Verify the prompt-structure and limits framing. Primary sources: Dupple 2026 ChatGPT-for-marketing guide; ClickUp marketing use-cases; OpenAI Academy.

topics.titleTr: Tek İçerik, Tüm Kanallar: AI ile Yeniden Kullan
topics.titleEn: One Post, Every Channel: AI Repurposing
topics.angle: checklist|a repeatable checklist to turn one strong piece into assets for every channel with AI.
topics.brief: Open with the insight that the biggest AI time-save in marketing is reformatting one strong piece across channels, not generating from scratch. A checklist-style evergreen: pick the hero asset; extract the core argument; derive a newsletter, a LinkedIn carousel, an X thread, an Instagram caption and a short-video script; adapt tone per platform; add a human polish and fact-check pass; schedule. Keep it channel-text repurposing (not video-to-shorts). Verify the 'repurpose beats generate' framing. Primary sources: Upwork ChatGPT-in-marketing; WebFX use-cases; Brevo ChatGPT-for-marketers.

topics.titleTr: Okur AI Metnini Anlıyor: Güveni Geri Kazan
topics.titleEn: Readers Can Smell AI Copy. Win Trust Back
topics.angle: mistakes|the tells that expose AI copy and how to edit for credibility and voice.
topics.brief: Contrarian push against publish-as-generated. Sections: the data that skepticism is rising (Metricool: the share of marketers saying AI performs worse than human work rose from 5% in 2025 to 14% in 2026); the tells (hedging, symmetrical lists, no specifics, no POV); an editing pass that adds first-hand detail, real examples, opinion and rhythm; disclosure and the platform AI-label trend. Verify the 5%-to-14% figure. Primary sources: Metricool ChatGPT-for-marketing report; Dupple mistakes section.

topics.brief: A reader-first filter on CES 2026.
